findings.title: Slots inside a date override return early and skip the busy-time check, allowing double bookings
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when a host has a date override on the slot's date and the slot falls inside the override window, the new `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` returns "available" before the `busy.every(...)` check at the bottom of the function ever runs. checkIfIsAvailable is the only place busy times (calendar events and existing bookings) are consulted — getTimeSlots never sees them. Consequence: for any host with a date override on a given day (fixed hosts via the new fixed-host filter, round-robin hosts via the loose-host filter, and single-user events since users default to isFixed), all of their existing bookings and calendar conflicts on that day are ignored, so the slot is offered and the host can be double-booked. Before this PR the busy check always ran, so this is a regression. The override-branch should fall through to the busy check instead of returning true.

findings.title: Working-hours gate fails open when the host has no working hours on the slot's day
findings.body: The new working-hours check treats a slot as "within working hours" whenever `workingHours.find(...)` returns undefined. The find callback only returns true when a workingHour entry matches the slot's UTC day AND the slot is outside its range; if the host has no working-hour entry at all for that weekday (their day off), the callback returns undefined for every entry, find returns undefined, the `return false` is skipped, and the host is considered available. For round-robin events, slots are generated from the union of all hosts' hours, so a slot on a fixed host's day off (generated from a round-robin host who works that day) passes the fixed-host filter and becomes bookable — exactly the kind of booking this PR is meant to prevent. The check should fail closed: if no workingHour covers the slot's day, the slot should be unavailable.

findings.title: Copy-paste bug: `end` is computed from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
findings.body: In the working-hours check, `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` duplicates the `start` computation — it was clearly meant to use slotEndTime. As a result `end > workingHour.endTime` can only fire when the slot's start is already past the end of working hours, and a slot that starts within working hours but ends after the host's availability end is treated as available. Example: fixed host works until 17:00, a round-robin co-host works until 19:00, and a 60-minute slot starts at 16:45 (aligned to the co-host's schedule) — the fixed host gets booked 16:45–17:45 despite being unavailable after 17:00.

findings.title: Date-override containment check accepts slots that only partially overlap the override
findings.body: The new override-range logic only rejects slots that are entirely outside the override: it returns "not within" when slotEndTime <= override.start or when slotStartTime > override.end. Two cases slip through and are treated as within the override (and therefore available): (1) a slot that starts before the override start but ends inside it, because slotStartTime.isBefore(override.start) is never checked; (2) a slot that starts before the override end but ends after it, because the end-side check is the strict `slotStartTime.isAfter(override.end)` — a slot starting at 17:30 with an override ending 18:00 (and even a slot starting exactly at 18:00, since isAfter is not inclusive) passes. Hosts with non-aligned schedules (e.g., fixed host override 14:00–18:00, co-host hours starting at :30) can be booked partially or fully outside their override window. The check should require the slot to be fully contained: slotStartTime >= override.start && slotEndTime <= override.end.

findings.title: `===` comparison between two Dayjs objects is always false (dead blocked-day branch)
findings.body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares object references, so it is never true — the author presumably meant `.isSame()`. This branch is meant to detect a fully blocked day (an override whose start equals its end, typically midnight, which is how "unavailable" date overrides are stored). Because it never fires, blocked days are only rejected incidentally via the surrounding before/after checks, and a slot starting exactly at the start==end timestamp of a blocked-day override (e.g., exactly 00:00 UTC) is reported as available on a day the host marked unavailable.

findings.title: Timezone conversion of date overrides drops the date component; overrides land on the wrong invitee day when timezones straddle midnight
findings.body: The new conversion shifts the stored override time by (inviteeOffset - organizerOffset) and then reads only `.hour()`/`.minute()`, discarding any day rollover, and the `activeOverrides` filter (line 207) still matches the override's stored-as-UTC date against the invitee's calendar day. When the organizer's and invitee's local dates differ, the override is applied on the wrong invitee day and never on the correct one. Concrete example: organizer in Honolulu (UTC-10) with an override Mar 10 08:00–09:00, invitee in Auckland (UTC+13). The true window is Mar 11 07:00–08:00 Auckland time, but the code offers Mar 10 07:00–08:00 Auckland (offset +1380 min rolls 08:00 to 07:00 the next day, and .hour() truncates it back onto Mar 10), while for inviteeDate Mar 11 the filter no longer matches the stored Mar 10 date so the override is missing entirely. The same happens for e.g. Tokyo organizer / Los Angeles invitee. This is the timezone-adjustment scenario the PR sets out to fix, still broken for large timezone gaps.

findings.title: dayjs.tz(override.timeZone) silently falls back to the server's timezone when timeZone is undefined
findings.body: TimeRange.timeZone is optional (packages/types/schedule.d.ts marks it `timeZone?: string`), and getSlots is a shared library function, but the new code calls `dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone)` unconditionally. When timeZone is undefined, dayjs.tz does not throw — it falls back to the runtime's local timezone (typically UTC on servers/containers). The offset calculation then becomes inviteeOffset - serverOffset instead of inviteeOffset - organizerOffset, silently shifting the override's slots for any caller that passes date overrides without a timeZone. Either make the field required for date overrides or handle the undefined case explicitly.

findings.title: No test covers the headline fix: date overrides of fixed hosts in round-robin events
findings.body: The PR's primary change is the new fixed-host/loose-host availability enforcement in checkIfIsAvailable (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts), but the only added test exercises a single-user event with a date override viewed from a different invitee timezone. There is no ROUND_ROBIN scenario with an isFixed host that has a date override, and no scenario where a host with a date override also has busy times/bookings on the override day — which is why the regression where the busy check is skipped on override days (the `dateOverrideExist` early return) is not caught: the new test would pass even with that bug. Please add tests for a round-robin event with a fixed host override (including timezones where organizer/invitee dates differ) and for a host with an override plus a conflicting booking on the same day.
